chunks: People discussed the matter of futuwwah in the presence of al-Sadiq عليه السلام, so he said: “Do you suppose that the matter of futuwwah is in immorality and debauchery? Futuwwah and muru'ah are only food set out, generosity bestowed through something recognized as good, and harm withheld. As for that, it is mere roguery and immorality.”

Then he said: “What is muru'ah?” The people said: “We do not know.” He said: “Muru'ah, by Allah, is that a man places his table in the courtyard of his house. Muru'ah is of two kinds: muru'ah in residence and muru'ah in travel. As for that which is in residence: recitation of the Qur'an, frequenting the mosques, walking with brothers in fulfilling needs, and having blessing seen upon the servant such that it gladdens the friend and suppresses the enemy. And as for that which is in travel: abundance of provisions and their goodness, giving them to those with you, your concealing the people’s matter after your parting from them, and much humor in other than what angers Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.”

Then he عليه السلام said: “By the One who sent my grandfather صلى الله عليه وآله with the truth as a Prophet, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, surely provides for the servant according to the measure of muru'ah. Assistance descends according to the measure of burden, and patience descends according to the measure of the intensity of affliction.”

key_terms.الزَّادِ: travel provisions shared generously with companions
key_terms.الْبَلَاءِ: affliction or trial, in proportion to which patience descends
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, whose recitation is part of muru'ah
key_terms.الْمَسَاجِدِ: the mosques, whose regular attendance reflects honorable conduct
key_terms.الْمُرُوءَةُ: manly virtue, dignity, and honorable conduct

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about futuwwah and muru'ah?
ai.summary: This hadith defines futuwwah and muru'ah as noble character expressed through generosity, hospitality, service, restraint from harm, and upright conduct in both residence and travel. It rejects the false idea that manliness lies in vice or reckless behavior, and teaches that divine provision, help, and patience correspond to a person's moral burden and affliction.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.2498 - People were discussing the concept of futuwwah (chivalry) in the presence of Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), and Imam (as) said:
"Do you think that futuwwah is about immorality and corruption? Futuwwah and manliness (muru'ah) are about presenting food, offering generosity with what is well-known, and refraining from causing harm. As for those actions you describe, they are recklessness and immorality."

Then Imam (as) asked: "What is muru'ah?"
The people replied: "We do not know."
Imam (as) said: "Muru'ah, by Allah (swt), is for a person to set their table in the open courtyard of their house. Muru'ah is of two kinds: muru'ah in settled life and muru'ah in travel.
As for muru'ah in settled life, it includes reciting the Quran, frequenting mosques, walking with one’s brothers to fulfill their needs, and showing kindness to servants such that it pleases friends and suppresses enemies.
As for muru'ah in travel, it includes taking ample and good provisions, sharing them with one’s companions, keeping the matters of the group confidential after parting from them, and engaging in frequent humor that does not anger Allah (swt), the Mighty and Glorious."

Then Imam (as) added: "By the One who sent my grandfather (peace and blessings of Allah (swt) be upon him and his family) as a Prophet with the truth, Allah (swt) provides for a servant in proportion to their muru'ah. Aid descends in proportion to the burden of responsibility, and patience descends in proportion to the severity of the trial."
